title: RIOT OS LibGen Configuration
description: Specification of configuration files for RIOT OS LibGen. Can be used as reference and for validation to specify which C host functions to export. If not specified otherwise, the names of things should be unqiue and alpha-numeric with underscores, not starting with a number.

libraries.description: Object whose properties represent libraries, or in other words collections of functions, constants et cetera that belong together and therefore should be exported in the same namespace or with the same prefix, for example. The property name is the name of a library.

^[a-z][a-z0-9\\_]+[a-z0-9]$.description: Object whose properties represent the contents of a library, such as functions, function handles, pointer handles, constants et cetera.

prefix.description: String that is used instead of the library name as prefix for the names of exported functions and constants in the WASM runtime environment. In JS, functions and constants are properties of the library object instead.

includes.description: List of strings that contain the (relative) paths to C header files to be included by the generated export code, so that the host C functions are available to it.

modules.description: List of strings that contain the names of RIOT OS modules required for the export code to be linked against the underlying C host functions.

packages.description: List of strings that contain the names of RIOT OS packages required for the export code to be linked against the underlying C host functions.

functions.description: Object whose properties represent functions that shall be exported by the generated code. The property name is the name of the function to be used from within the runtime environment.

anyOf.description: Object whose properties define the function signature (parameters, return type, name of the original function, ...) in LibGen format, which should fit the original function and will also be used to generate function signatures for the runtime environment.

original_name.description: String that contains the name of the C host function to export. If not specified, the property name of the object representing the function will be used.

parameters.description: Object whose properties represent the parameters input to a function. The property name is the parameter's name.

anyOf.description: Shortcut for representation of a function that has no parameters. String that contains the return type of the function. The name of the original C host function will be derived from the function name.
Shortcut for representation of a function that has no parameters and no return type. The name of the original C host function will be derived from the function name.

function_handles.description: Object whose properties represent function handles that can be used similarly to function pointers. The property name is the name of the function handle.

anyOf.description: Object whose properties represent the signature (parameters, return type) of functions associated to a function handle.

parameters.description: Object whose properties represent the parameters input to a function corresponding to a function handle. The property name is the name of the parameter.

anyOf.description: Shortcut for representation of a function handle that has no parameters and no return type.

pointer_handles.description: Object whose properties represent pointer handles that can be used similarly to void pointers. The property name is the name of the pointer handle.

anyOf.description: Object whose properties define the pointer handle.

type.description: String with the full C type of the underlying pointer. This is not limited to LibGen primitives and must not be a function or pointer handle name, and the type is only used for casting internally.

max_entries.description: Number of pointers of this type that can be handed out to the runtime environment at the same time (default: 10).

anyOf.description: Shortcut for a pointer handle with default options. String with the full C type of the underlying pointer.

constants.description: Object whose properties represent constants that can be used similarly to C pre-processor defines. The property name is the name of the constant.

^[a-z][a-z0-9\\_]+[a-z0-9]$.description: String or number with the constant value. This cannot be a macro or an expression or anything other than a string or a number.

structs.description: Object whose properties represent structs that can be passed between the host and the runtime environment by value. The property name is the name of the struct, which can be used as a type.

^[a-z][a-z0-9\\_]+[a-z0-9]$.description: Object whose properties define the struct.

type.description: String with the C type of the struct.

allocatable.description: Whether the runtime can create (and free) instances of the struct, which live on the host until they are freed. Instances are referenced by handles, and can be passed to parameters that are pointers to the struct (e.g. my_struct*).

fields.description: Object whose properties represent the fields of the struct that are exposed. The property name is the name of the field.

arrays.description: Object whose properties represent named arrays with homogeneous element type and static size (e.g. buffers). The property name is the name of the array, which can be used for pointer parameters (e.g. my_array* or const my_array*).

anyOf.description: Object whose properties define the array.

allocatable.description: Whether the runtime can create (and free) instances of the array, which live on the host until they are freed. Instances are referenced by handles, and can be passed to parameters that are pointers to the array (e.g. my_array*).

array_type.description: String with the element type and the static size of the array. The element type can be a primitive, a pointer handle or a struct.

allocatable.description: Either a boolean, or an object with options.

new.description: Name of the function for creating instances (default: new_<name>).

free.description: Name of the function for freeing instances (default: free_<name>).

max_entries.description: Number of instances that can exist at the same time (default: 10).

anyOf.description: String that contains the primitive type of the parameter, if it is of primitive type. The type can either be a primitive as listed in the end of the specification, or a function handle, or a pointer handle.
String that contains the name of a function or pointer handle, if the parameter is a function or pointer handle.
Object whose properties represent a parameter.
String that contains the primitive type of the parameter, if it is of primitive type.
String that contains the name of a function or pointer handle, if the parameter is a function or pointer handle.

length_parameter.description: String that contains the name of another parameter that is used to pass the length of the byte array that is passed as another parameter. Only needed for parameters of type byte array.

direction.description: Whether the parameter is passed to the host function (in, the default), or filled by the host function (out). For output parameters, the C type is a pointer to the given type, except for arrays and byte arrays. In JS, an object (or an array for arrays) needs to be passed that is filled after the call; values of primitives, pointer handles, strings and byte arrays are put into its property value.

anyOf.description: String that contains the primitive return type, if it is of primitive type.
String that contains the name of a pointer handle, if the return type is a pointer handle.
